clue.text: Society group entertained by genial farmer

indicators.note: something entertained by a host is taken in, so the society group sits inside the word for genial

parts.note: human in the old sense of humane, kindly and warm
a band is a group of musicians or people

explanation.surface: A club or society is welcomed by a friendly man who works the land.
explanation.definitionFit: A husbandman is an old-fashioned word for someone who cultivates land and keeps animals, a farmer by another name.

clue.text: Maybe saw newspaper columnist?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to cut roughly, as one might with a saw, so sawing is one kind of ...
a journalist, especially a jobbing one writing for a paper

explanation.surface: Perhaps a proverb from a writer of a newspaper column.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like a proverb or saying, which a columnist might trot out, but here it is the cutting verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: hacking is rough chopping with a blade, and a hack is a workaday journalist.

clue.text: One good 'iding light under a bushel? Blunder

parts.note: a saint is one good person, abbreviated ST

indicators.note: the dropped H of the Cockney-style ''iding' tells you to drop the H from the following word too

parts.note: hiding one's light under a bushel means being modest, so humble

explanation.surface: A modest saint who hides their talents makes a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'hide your light under a bushel' means conceal your abilities, i.e. be humble; the aitchless ''iding' asks for ''UMBLE', as Dickens's Uriah Heep says it.
explanation.definitionFit: To stumble is to trip up or make a mistake, the same as to blunder.

clue.text: Writer I squashed, I being held to be right

parts.note: an author is a writer

indicators.note: a thing being held is clasped inside, so the second I sits within the word for squashed

parts.note: sat on means squashed, as one might sit on a hat

explanation.surface: A writer says they were crushed but held to be in the right.
explanation.definitionFit: Authorisation is permission, a right granted to do something.

clue.text: Recognises research establishment must be placed in East Anglian town

indicators.note: being placed in a town means going inside its name, so the research body goes within it

parts.note: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, East Anglia
CERN is the European particle physics laboratory near Geneva

explanation.surface: A research lab is told it must relocate to a Norfolk market town.
explanation.walkthrough: DISS is a small town in Norfolk, in the East Anglia region of England.
explanation.definitionFit: To discern something is to perceive or make it out, which is to recognise it.

clue.text: A wide wood becomes flooded

parts.note: W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide
ash is a timber, the wood of the ash tree

explanation.surface: A broad forest turns into a waterlogged swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Awash means covered with water, swamped, which is to say flooded.

clue.text: Nitrogen-free exhaust blasted

indicators.note: being free of something means lacking it, so the nitrogen symbol comes out

parts.note: to spend energy or resources is to exhaust them
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Exhaust fumes without nitrogen were blown out.
explanation.definitionFit: To blast along is to travel at great speed, so blasted and sped both mean raced.

clue.text: Material obtained from model, one nabbed by copper

indicators.note: something nabbed by a policeman is held inside him, so these letters go within the abbreviation

parts.note: PC, police constable, is a copper
a last is the shoemaker's model of a foot
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Stuff taken from a model and one item seized by a policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Plastic is a synthetic substance used for making things, a material.

clue.text: Trade's idea to work out the essential elements

indicators.note: letters set to work out are being reworked into a new order

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored and the S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A trade's notion is to figure out what is truly essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata are things wanted or needed, the essentials, from the Latin for things desired.

clue.text: Irritable, lacking yen at the end for living

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the yen letter is removed
this places the removed letter at the end of the word

parts.note: crusty means short-tempered or irritable
Y is the abbreviation for the yen, Japan's currency

explanation.surface: Someone grumpy for want of money at the end of the month, trying to make a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn a crust is idiomatic for earning one's living, the crust standing for a livelihood.

clue.text: Tongue-twisting clergyman's to be corseted for flights

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner famously swapped the first sounds of words, so swap the opening sounds here

parts.note: to be corseted is to wear stays, the stiffened bodice of old
stays is the old word for a corset

explanation.surface: A tongue-tied vicar's flights of fancy about being laced into a corset.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the opening sounds of WEAR STAYS to get 'stair ways'; stays are an old corset.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of stairs is a staircase, so flights are stairways.

clue.text: Shuffling back over mountains, chaps start to tire

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a chain of mountains
chaps are men

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A shuffle back over mountains and men start to flag.
explanation.definitionFit: Shuffling cards or papers means putting them in a new order, which is a reordering by another name.

clue.text: It could be the dear that's badly hurt

parts.note: the words the dear, when broken up and rearranged, can give the letters of the second word, so the answer read as wordplay describes them

explanation.surface: A beloved one who has been badly wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: HEARTED broken, i.e. rearranged, gives THE DEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply grieved or emotionally crushed is wounded in spirit, sorely hurt.

clue.text: Marches as gangster leading another baddy into grottoes?

indicators.note: going into the caves means being put inside that word

parts.note: grottoes are caves

indicators.note: leading means coming first, so the gangster precedes the other villain

parts.note: Al Capone, the Chicago gangster, gives AL
a cad is a dishonourable man, a baddy

explanation.surface: A mobster leading another villain into caves, marching in procession.
explanation.definitionFit: A cavalcade is a procession, originally of riders, so cavalcades are parades or marches.

clue.text: Sort of medicine that gives a patient hesitation for a time

indicators.note: one thing given for another replaces it, so the hesitation sound swaps in

parts.note: a patient is someone under medical care
A plus T, the abbreviation for time
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A medicine which makes a sick person pause for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperient is a laxative, a mild medicine that opens the bowels.

clue.text: This shopkeeper is said to be more stupid

indicators.note: being said means spoken, so the word sounds like the stupid comparative

parts.note: gross can mean dense or dull, so grosser is more stupid

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper rumoured to be thicker than the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper selling food and household goods.

clue.text: You may see ______ your bird table, Anne?

definitions.text: You may see ______ your bird table
definitions.meaning: the gap is filled by ..., the redbreasts perched on the table
Anne ... is the British TV presenter of The Weakest Link

explanation.surface: Anne is asked whether she sees birds on her bird table.
explanation.walkthrough: ANNE ROBINSON is a British TV presenter, famous for The Weakest Link; split the answer to fill the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the presenter Anne, and the words robins on read as two words in the gap.

clue.text: One fruit topped with another

indicators.note: a word topped has its head cut off, losing its first letter

parts.note: another fruit, here bananas

explanation.surface: One piece of fruit with another placed on top of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ananas is the pineapple, or the plant it grows on, a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Charge to go up

parts.note: the fee paid for going up in an aeroplane, though charge to go up suggests a rise in price

explanation.surface: A fee or price that is about to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rising price; the real sense is what you pay to take to the air.
explanation.definitionFit: The fare for a flight is the price charged to travel by air.

clue.text: Unhappy players at Bangor?

parts.note: Bangor is a town in County Down, Northern Ireland
the cast is the set of players in a show

explanation.surface: Actors at Bangor looking glum.
explanation.walkthrough: There are Bangors in Wales and Northern Ireland; the one in County Down, Northern Ireland, is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast means low in spirits, dejected, so unhappy.

clue.text: Ring girl that's texted you with unending desire

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
in text messages you is written U

indicators.note: unending means the last letter is removed

parts.note: lust is strong desire

explanation.surface: A girl texts a message of endless longing to someone she loves.
explanation.definitionFit: An annulus is a ring-shaped figure, from the Latin for little ring.

clue.text: A bishop in epic region recreated Homer

indicators.note: something recreated is made anew, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop in the region of the epic recreates Homer's poems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' wants to be the Greek poet of epics; it is a homing bird. The A and RR sit within the anagram pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, bred to fly back home, the kind once used to carry messages.

clue.text: Skittish, losing head, insecure

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: frisky means lively and skittish

explanation.surface: A nervy, skittish creature loses its head and feels unsafe.
explanation.definitionFit: Risky means dangerous, not safe, and so insecure.

clue.text: Raised cash, but article's not secured

indicators.note: not secured means not kept, so the article is let go

parts.note: bread is slang for money
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Money was raised, but an item was not secured.
explanation.definitionFit: Bred means brought up, as children are raised.

clue.text: A 'dosing' is arranged — after this?

indicators.note: letters arranged are set in a new order here

explanation.surface: A course of medicine is set up, following a doctor's verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: treatment is arranged after the doctor identifies the illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnosis is the doctor's identification of an illness, which comes before prescribing a treatment.

clue.text: Mathematician replacing first item of geometer's equipment?

indicators.note: the first letter of the tool is swapped for another letter

parts.note: a ruler is part of a geometry set

explanation.surface: A mathematician swapping out the first piece of a geometry kit.
explanation.walkthrough: The replacement E is the mathematical constant e, named after this very mathematician, which the definition supplies.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonhard Euler was the great eighteenth-century Swiss mathematician.

clue.text: Entreated pretentious person audibly

indicators.note: audibly means as heard, so the word for a show-off is spoken aloud

parts.note: a pseud is a pretentious poseur

explanation.surface: A poseur begged loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue for peace is to beg or petition for it, so sued means pleaded.

clue.text: Isn't he dopy! (Possibly being this?)

indicators.note: possibly means the letters may be rearranged into another word

parts.note: the apostrophe is ignored

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a dozy man, wondering whether he is in a trance.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: someone in a trance looks dopy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnotised means put into a trance, which leaves a person looking dazed and dopy.
